abstract: Maintains underwater acoustic signatures, scientific instrument specifications, and dry laboratory workspace records
system_message:
You are Oceanographic science operations lead (OSC). The Oceanographic science operations lead (OSC) maintains underwater acoustic signatures, scientific instrument specifications, and dry laboratory workspace records, along with underway atmospheric observation logs for candidate research vessels.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Underway atmospheric observation（METEO）
information_points.content:
OSC-METEO-2HT：Sensor calibration logs for the surface boundary-layer meteorological mast suite on RV Bathyal Horizon record an automated meteorological mast sampling rate of 2 Hz.
OSC-METEO-FS5：Calibration records for the surface boundary-layer meteorological mast suite on RV Pelagic Explorer indicate an automated meteorological mast sampling rate of 5 Hz.
OSC-METEO-KSD：For RV Oceanus Surveyor, sensor calibration logs for the surface boundary-layer meteorological mast suite show an automated meteorological mast sampling rate of 1 Hz.

information_points.title: Maintains underwater acoustic signatures, scientific instrument specifications, and dry laboratory workspace records（OPS）
information_points.content:
OSC-OPS-LXN：For RV Bathyal Horizon, noise trial evaluations across the 10 Hz to 100 kHz spectrum determine that certified hydroacoustic acoustic silence is false. The vessel general arrangement deck plan indicates an enclosed climate-controlled scientific dry laboratory area of 105 m2.
OSC-OPS-SAP：For RV Oceanus Surveyor, hull acoustic noise trials across the 10 Hz to 100 kHz frequency bands confirm that certified hydroacoustic acoustic silence is true under international survey standards. The general arrangement deck plan documents a scientific dry laboratory area of 75 m2 of enclosed climate-controlled workspace for computing consoles and sensor telemetry.
OSC-OPS-UE3：For RV Pelagic Explorer, acoustic survey range noise trials across the 10 Hz to 100 kHz frequency bands confirm that certified hydroacoustic acoustic silence is true, meeting radiated underwater noise limits for fisheries and seabed survey standards. The vessel general arrangement deck plan specifies a usable scientific dry laboratory area of 75 m2 across its enclosed climate-controlled dry instrumentation spaces.
